```suggestion
@client.tree.context_menu(name='Show Join Date')
```

Considering context menu commands can have spaces in the name, might as well.

```suggestion
# A Context Menu command is an app command that can be run on a member or on a message by 
# accessing a menu within the client, usually via right clicking.
```

```suggestion
# It always takes an interaction as its first parameter and a Member or Message as its second parameter.
```

The union note is incorrect, it supports `Union[discord.User, discord.Member]`, but this is pretty niche usage so no point in mentioning it since it makes the sentence awkward.

```suggestion
# This context menu command only works on members
```

```suggestion
    # The format_dt function formats the date time into a human readable representation in the official client
    await interaction.response.send_message(f'{member} joined in {discord.utils.format_dt(member.joined_at)}')
```

Might as well turn this into a human readable date.

```suggestion
@client.tree.context_menu(name='Report to Moderators')
```

Sticking with title case here.

```suggestion
# This context menu command only works on messages
```

```suggestion
        f'Thanks for reporting this message by {message.author.mention} to our moderators.', ephemeral=True
```

```suggestion
    url_view.add_item(discord.ui.Button(label='Go to Message', style=discord.ButtonStyle.url, url=message.jump_url))
```

Title case nit again.

Not that I think this example should be used as-is but maybe it'd be "cooler" to also make an embed with the message information. Something like this:

```py
embed = discord.Embed(title='Reported Message')
if message.content:
    embed.description = message.content

embed.set_author(name=message.author.display_name, icon_url=message.author.display_avatar.url)
embed.timestamp = message.created_at
```

It gives it a bit more "flavour" I suppose.
